Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Agency on any matter listed on the agenda or on any
other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk
Municipal Code. If you wish to address the Agency, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to
Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. The Agency will hear public comment on items listed
on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Agency will hear public comment on matters
not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or
unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Agency may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule
certain matters for consideration at a future Agency meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Agency:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Agency as a whole and not directed to individual Agency Members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the
agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons
with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the
City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Agency regarding any item on this agenda after it
has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.,
every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

SUBJECT:  RECOGNIZED OBLIGATION PAYMENT SCHEDULE FOR THE FISCAL
  PERIOD COMMENCING JULY 1, 2024 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025

Background:

Pursuant to Section 34177 of the Health and Safety Code (HSC), the Successor Agency must
prepare a Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule annually, listing the anticipated payments
for enforceable obligations to be made from July 1 through the following June 30.

Attached is the Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (Successor Agency)
Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS 24-25) for the fiscal year ending June 30,
2025. Resolution No. OB 24-01 approving ROPS 24-25, containing this information was
presented before the Los Angeles County Fourth Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight
Board (Oversight Board) today.

The Oversight Board must approve all ROPS. Furthermore, each Oversight Board-approved
ROPS must be submitted to the Department of Finance (DOF) for review.

The preparation and submittal of ROPS 23-24 are for allowing the Successor Agency to pay its
enforceable obligations for the period from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. HSC Section 34177
requires the Successor Agency to submit an Oversight Board-approved ROPS 24-25 to the DOF
and to the County Auditor-Controller no later than February 1, 2024.

The DOF may eliminate or modify any item on the ROPS before approving the ROPS. The DOF
must make its determination regarding the enforceable obligations and the amount and funding
source for each enforceable obligation listed on ROPS 24-25 no later than April 15, 2024. Within
five business days of the DOF’s determination, the Successor Agency may request to “meet and
confer” with the DOF on disputed items. The DOF will issue its final determination after the meet
and confer.
 Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment  January 16, 2024
Agency  Page No. 2
Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule FY 24-25

The County Auditor-Controller is required to make Redevelopment Property Tax Trust Fund
(RPTTF) disbursements to the Successor Agency pursuant to the DOF-approved ROPS 24-25
on June 1, 2024 (to cover enforceable obligation payments from July 1, 2024 through December
31, 2024) and January 2, 2025 (to cover enforceable obligation payments from January 1, 2025
through June 30, 2025).

The Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (SA) fiscal year 2024/25
enforceable obligations total $7,949,049 which are 82% funded ($6,267,549) from RPTTF. The
SA is presently negotiating with the County of Los Angeles the disposal of the last remaining
property, the Judges’ Parking Structure.

Background:

Pursuant to 34177(j) of the California Health and Safety Code (HSC), the Successor Agency is
required to prepare a proposed administrative budget for each six-month fiscal period, which
must be submitted to the Oversight Board for approval and the total administrative budget
covering the entire fiscal year cannot exceed $250,000. Each proposed administrative budget
must include all of the following: (1) estimated amounts for Successor Agency administrative
costs for the applicable six-month fiscal period; (2) proposed sources of payment for the
administrative costs; and (3) proposals for arrangements for administrative and operations
services provided by the City of Norwalk or another entity.

Attached is the Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (Successor Agency)
proposed Administrative Budgets for the six-month fiscal periods from July 1, 2024 through
December 31, 2024 and January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2025. Resolution OB 24-02
approving administrative budgets will be presented before the Los Angeles County Fourth
Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board on January 16, 2024.

The attached administrative budget covering the entire fiscal year 2024/25 complies with the
above listed requirements.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. SA 24-01 - FACSIMILE SIGNATURES

Background:

Government Code §5501 provides that any authorized officer may, after filing with the Secretary
of State his manual signature certified by him under oath, execute or cause to be executed,
certain documents including any instrument of payment, with a facsimile signature in lieu of a
manual signature. Following the filing of the facsimile signature with the Secretary of State,
banks may be directed to honor all checks, drafts, and warrants when bearing those signatures
and facsimile signatures.

This resolution authorizes banks to honor checks, drafts and warrants bearing the manual or
facsimile signatures of Chair Margarita L. Rios plus the manual or facsimile signature of Jana
Stuard, Finance Officer.

   RESOLUTION NO. SA 24-01

  A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING
  CERTAIN BANKS TO HONOR ALL CHECKS, DRAFTS, AND
  WARRANTS WHEN BEARING CERTAIN SIGNATURES AND
  FACSIMILE SIGNATURES OF AGENCY OFFICIALS AND RESCINDING
  ALL CONFLICTING RESOLUTIONS

  WHEREAS, the Agency has certain Banks as depositories of Agency Funds; and

  WHEREAS, the Agency Board determines that it is necessary for the efficient
administration of the fiscal affairs of the Agency that this Resolution be passed and
adopted.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS
FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. Each depository of the Successor Agency to the Norwalk
Redevelopment Agency of the City of Norwalk, be and it is hereby requested, authorized
and directed to honor all checks, drafts, warrants or other orders for the payment of money
drawn in the name of the Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency of
the City of Norwalk on all of its accounts when bearing or purporting to bear the manual
or facsimile signature of Chair Margarita L. Rios plus the manual or facsimile signature of
Jana Stuard, Finance Officer.

  Section 2. Said banks, including their correspondent banks, shall be entitled to
honor and to charge the Agency for all such checks, warrants, drafts, or other orders for
the payment of money, regardless of by whom or by what means the actual or purported
facsimile signature or signatures thereon may have been affixed thereto, if such facsimile
signature or signatures resemble the facsimile specimens filed with said bank by the
Secretary of the Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency of the City of
Norwalk.

  Section 3. All previous Resolutions authorizing the honoring of signatures and
facsimile signatures of Agency officials other than those set forth in this Resolution are
hereby rescinded.

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 16th day of January 2024.

  MARGARITA L. RIOS
  CHAIR
